summary: Missouri Conservation Commission tower site in Ozark County: towersite acquired 1951-52, tower erected 1954-55, fire in 1974. No source found on the site today.

events.note: Towersite acquired, recorded in the Missouri Conservation Commission annual report for fiscal 1951-52. The report gives no month.
A new tower was erected at Romance, recorded in the annual report for fiscal 1954-55. The report gives no month.
August 14, 1974 fire near the Romance towersite, close to West Plains. A snake shorted an electric fence and started it. The fire is near the towersite, not documented as at the tower.

evidence.supports: new tower erected at Romance, fiscal 1954-55
evidence.quote: A new tower was erected at Romance in Ozark County.

evidence.supports: fire near the towersite, near West Plains
evidence.quote: The most unusual cause of a fire, perhaps in history, happened near Romanse Towersite near West Plains.

evidence.supports: snake shorted fence and started a blaze
evidence.quote: A snake, crawling up a fence post, shorted out an electric fence and started a blaze.

evidence.supports: the account comes from The Chillicothe Constitution-Tribune

notes_for_editor: Only the Central US Lookouts page was read; it quotes the Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports and a 1974 newspaper item. Fiscal-year entries use the first calendar year of the range (1951, 1954), and the notes say so. The 1974 fire is recorded near the towersite, not at the tower. The source spells the site 'Romanse'. Status, access and today's condition were not found, and the web search budget was exhausted before annual reports or Missouri newspapers could be checked.
